verdicts.quote: N is the attacker's decimal literal, so `?p[arr][2000000000]=x` grows `result` to 2e9 interface headers (~32 GB) before any schema rule - maxItems, maxLength, type - is consulted.
verdicts.why: Same defect by mechanism. N11 names the exact sink the advisory names - sliceMapToSlice at openapi3filter/req_resp_decoder.go:936/953 - and states the mechanism the advisory states: the deepObject bracket index is parsed with strconv.Atoi with no upper bound, max is taken over attacker-chosen keys, and the loop `for i := 0; i <= max; i++` allocates one slot per position up to that index, with a second slice of the same length at :986. It explicitly places the allocation before the schema's own limits (maxItems) are applied, and characterises the impact as unauthenticated single-request memory exhaustion / OOM. Line reference (:953 vs the advisory's :936) is inside the same function and does not change the verdict. Other findings in the same file (N07 deepSet type-assertion panic, N08 nil Items dereference, N09 unbounded io.ReadAll of the body, N10 zip bomb / buffer append) are different defects and were not used.
